title: Weekly BIM coordination of a federated cloud project: collect, check, correct, report, archive
intent: Keep a federated cloud project current in one weekly session: collect model data in an unattended batch, add LOIN completeness and a clash run, check everything against fixed rules and last week's snapshot, repair what is safe to repair, queue the rest for approval, and publish one dashboard report with recommendations for the team.

sequence.do: Preflight: Revit idle at Home with no model open (ask before closing the user's work), bridge alive, disk and collaboration cache space, registry compared with the cloud folder (new or renamed models), report folder REPORTS/<date> created
sequence.without_tool: registry as a plain CSV of model name, project and model GUIDs

sequence.do: Collect in batch (unattended): Model Health Check and PBP + Worksets report over all registry models, then Export Schedules (instance parameters, project information, sheet list); output folder typed explicitly
sequence.tools: ZEN ACC Gate started by PostCommand
sequence.without_tool: bridge script that opens each cloud model with link worksets closed and writes the same fields (warnings by type, views, sheets, links, groups, levels, grids) and the schedule rows

sequence.do: Collect deep, read-only: shared position at the internal origin per model against the authority, link instances per host with workset and total transform (links loaded, not from the batch report), Project Information keys, standard schedules present
LOIN snapshot: from the exported instance-parameter schedules count filled values per model, category and field (family elements only); score against the client's LOIN table, or state the assumption
sequence.without_tool: schedule export by ViewSchedule.Export from the bridge

sequence.do: Clash run: open the discipline models in one session (link worksets closed), intersect the agreed category pairs, separate penetrations, group clashes, owner by routing priority; close the models unsaved. Use the cloud clash service instead where the project has one
sequence.without_tool: cloud coordination service export (tracked clash groups)

sequence.do: Check: one dataset per source (models, links, warnings, LOIN, clashes) keyed by model or pair and week; findings per model and rule; week-over-week deltas from the second week on

Correct: safe fixes automatically (repair links to the matrix, missing building name, missing standard schedules, then sync); anything that moves geometry, changes coordinates or deletes waits for the coordinator's approval
sequence.tools: ZEN ACC Gate (Create Cloud Links, Import Standard Schedules) or bridge

sequence.do: Report: one dashboard page in the standard report form ARPL-RPT-0001 (report/STANDARD.md: headline, tiles, recommendations, clashes, LOIN, warnings, checks, link matrix, model contents, not collected) over its five datasets; every number drawn from the datasets, none typed
sequence.tools: dashboard artifact from report/template/index.html over the report/datasets/ files (standard ARPL-RPT-0001)
sequence.without_tool: any BI tool reading the same CSVs

sequence.do: Print: one PDF booklet per model in the same unattended batch (ACC Gate 'Print PDFs from Print Intel workbooks'); set-up once per model: fixed print set, Print Intel workbook, PrintJobs row; check page counts against the sets and run the drift check when sheets change
sequence.tools: Revit print dialog, ZEN Export Print Intel and ACC Gate
sequence.without_tool: bridge PDF export per model with PDFExportOptions over the same print sets

sequence.do: Archive: keep raw outputs in REPORTS/<date>; append the week's datasets to history; submit new lessons to the ARPL inbox (Revit and ZEN alike)

rule_table.rule: Every host has each link its matrix defines, none missing or duplicated
Every link instance placed by shared coordinates; when all models share one coordinate system and one internal origin, the link transform is identity
Shared origin and angle equal the authority model, tolerance 0.01 ft
Building name equals the registry key; no template placeholder text
Count up more than 10% week over week, or a new warning type in a model's top five; week 1 is the baseline
No new hard clashes in the agreed pairs; open clash groups falling week over week; penetrations reported separately
Over 300 MB or up more than 15% in a week
Any family over 5 MB; in-place count rising

Filled ÷ required values of family elements in the instance-parameter schedule at or above the project target (95% placeholder) per model; required fields from the client's LOIN table, else every information column with the assumption stated
rule_table.fix: report; recommendations name the categories with the most missing values

rule_table.rule: Sheet numbers unique; sheets without views flagged
Links on their own link worksets; elements on the default workset below a set limit
Standard schedules and view templates present
Every model in the cloud folder has a registry row, and the reverse

data_model: Datasets keyed by ModelKey (or discipline pair) and SnapshotDate: models, links (host x link), warnings (model x rank), loin (model x category x field), clashes (element pair), findings (model x rule, calculated). Raw outputs per run in REPORTS/<date>; history appended per dataset.
decisions_for_the_user: The client's LOIN table: required fields per category and stage, and the target
The clash matrix: category pairs, hard or clearance, routing priority
Approval of every geometry, coordinate, workset or delete fix
discipline_authority: Discipline leads: content of their models; the routine reports, it does not redesign

results_recorded.note: Run end to end on 2026-10-27 on two projects: a 13-model campus (health, PBP, links, schedules) and the 6-model Snowdon Towers sample (all steps including LOIN and clash run). First weeks are baselines; trends start with the second run.
measured: ACC Gate health + PBP: 12 models, about 2 min, 8-11 s per open
ACC Gate Export Schedules: 6 models, 3 schedules each
Clash run: 5 models opened in 33 s; 9 pairs in about 3 min; 365 intersections -> 282 clashes in 74 groups + 83 penetrations
Batch cloud links: 156 links in 21 min (setup week)
Print sets and Print Intel set-up: 6 models, 139 sheets, about 20 min once; booklets checked page for page against the sets (2026-10-28)

report_form.note: One page, top to bottom. Every figure comes from a dataset or a calculation, never typed into the text; recommendations name owners but no numbers. Structure and data contract fixed as standard ARPL-RPT-0001 (report/STANDARD.md).
sections: Header: project, week, baseline or trend week; one sentence with checks passed, warnings and top warning type, LOIN completeness against target, hard clashes and groups
Tiles: LOIN completeness, hard clashes (with groups), warnings, checks passing, Revit links, views not on sheets, model groups
Recommendations for the team: ordered by impact, each with the owning team and the action; recurring causes first (one decision that clears many items)
Clashes: bars by discipline pair, bars by team that moves, table of the largest groups (pair, level, owner, main element with id)
LOIN: model x field grid of fill rates; categories ranked by missing values; system and analytical elements counted separately
Warnings: types across models (top five per model), warnings by model
Checks: one row per model, one column per rule (pass, fail, baseline, not collected)
Link matrix: host x link heat map (placed, workset, transform)
Model contents: health fields per model
Not collected this week: every gap and every assumption, in plain words

datasets.models: one row per model: health fields, shared position, link and workset counts, schedules present
datasets.links: host x link: instance, workset, transform, status
datasets.loin: model, category, element_kind, field, instances, filled
datasets.clashes: one row per element pair: pair, disciplines, kind, group, owner, categories, family and type, levels, ids and unique ids, volume, centroid
